summary: Quick frontend-only retest of player.tsx at 390x844 viewport, using MAC 18:41:B9:44:28:D3. I polled the overlay, the controls and the <video> state every second. PASS: on the first channel (A&E FHD H.265), the overlay clears at about 7s, right when currentTime starts moving. Controls stay visible while loading and auto-hide 4s after real playback starts. FAIL: after tapping Next, the second channel (A&E) reaches readyState 4 at about 6s but the video stays paused (currentTime 0). The overlay correctly keeps showing, but playback never starts. At 15s the start timeout moves to the next candidate (readyState goes back to 0). FAIL (minor): tapping play/pause while loading or paused hides the controls after 4s. The stall watchdog was only code-reviewed, not forced.

ui_bugs.issue: The second channel never starts. The video reaches readyState 4 at about 6s but stays paused, and the 'Sintonizando...' overlay stays up until the 15s timeout moves to the next candidate. RCA: expo-video web replace() never resets _status, which is still 'readyToPlay' from the previous channel. The status setter returns early when the value is the same (VideoPlayer.web.js:200), so the new source's canplay emits no statusChange. Your 'readyToPlay' -> player.play() recovery (player.tsx:94) therefore never runs for the second and later channels. The play() calls in replace() and after replaceAsync were ignored or aborted, so the video stays paused.
bumpControls() runs on every press, including while loading or paused. The controls hid 4s after tapping pause while the video was loading.
The icon uses isPlaying, which is stale-true on web (replace() sets playing=true). It shows 'pause' while the video is actually paused, during loading on the second channel.

action_items: Do not rely on statusChange 'readyToPlay' after a source change: it is not emitted on web when the old status was already readyToPlay. Fix: in the existing 2s watchdog interval (or a new 1s interval), call player.play() if phaseRef.current === 'loading' && fresh.current. On web, play() on a paused element is idempotent and harmless. Optionally also call it in the 'sourceChange' event.
Play/pause onPress: call player.play()/pause(), then bumpControls() only if real playback continues. Otherwise call setShowControls(true) and clear hideTimer.
Base the play/pause icon on real progress (phase === 'playing' && isPlaying), or track the pause state locally, instead of isPlaying alone.
critical_code_review_comments: player.tsx:94: the readyToPlay listener is the only recovery path for an aborted play(), and it never fires on the second and later channels on web.
player.tsx:218: bumpControls is called unconditionally on play/pause.

success_rate.frontend: 50% (first-channel overlay and loading-controls visibility pass; Next-channel playback fails; play/pause-while-loading hides controls)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Repro: set localStorage iptv_device_mac/pin and go to /browser. Tap the first [data-testid^=channel-item-] and poll every 1s for 16s: player-loading, player-play-pause-button, and video readyState/paused/currentTime. Then tap player-next-button and poll for 18s. Before the fix, the second channel reaches readyState 4 with paused=true and currentTime=0, the overlay stays up, and the video never plays.
rca_of_issue: expo-video web (VideoPlayer.web.js): replace() calls pause(), load() and play() but does not reset status. The status setter returns early when the value is the same, so 'readyToPlay' -> 'readyToPlay' emits nothing on the new source's canplay. The app's only re-play trigger is that statusChange, so the second channel stays paused at readyState 4 until START_TIMEOUT.
